text:
Alice: Heads up — proposing removal of the legacy auth header (`Authorization: Bearer-legacy`) from public SDKs on 2025-06-15. Need partner coordination and an escape hatch.
Ben: Timeline noted. We should ship a runtime flag + per-account allowlist and emit telemetry. Propose flag `enable_legacy_auth` + new header `X-RW-Legacy-Auth`.
Carlos: PartnerX still uses the legacy header in SI templates. They'll need ~12 weeks grace. Can we extend or provide an escape-hatch header they can set per-request?
Dana: Marketing wants a joint announcement window — two weeks after SDK stable cut. Also need partner comms doc and a single-page customer notice.
Ben: Implementation plan: add flag, default false, but SDKs log a deprecation warning when true. Example config: 
```
// SDK config
{ "enable_legacy_auth": false, "legacy_header": "X-RW-Legacy-Auth" }
```
Carlos: For PartnerX staging tests we'll need a checklist: auth modes (legacy-only, new-only, both), rotation, timeout edge-cases. They asked for an "escape-hatch" header they can flip without rebuilding.
Eva: Legal: we'll need deprecation language in partner agreements and a short TOS addendum. Also confirm no PII leakage if header value format changes during rotation.
Alice: Action items: 1) Dev: flag + telemetry (Ben) 2) Partner comms draft (Carlos + Dana) 3) Legal copy (Eva) 4) Marketplace note (partnerships). Can everyone confirm ETAs?
Ben: Dev ETA: PR by 2025-04-10, internal QA 2 weeks, canary right after. Will add `rw.legacy.auth_warning` metric and a deprecation log.
Carlos: PartnerX requests a test matrix. I'll own coordination and will ask their SI leads to run tests in our staging. Matrix items: 
- legacy header only
- new token header only
- both headers present (new wins)
- key rotation mid-session
- allowlist behavior

Ben: Server-side behavior: if both headers present, prefer new token. We'll accept `X-RW-Legacy-Auth: true` as a runtime escape-hatch ONLY for accounts on the allowlist. Pseudocode: `if (account.allowlist.legacy) { acceptLegacy() } else { reject() }`. We'll also tag telemetry `legacy.used=true`.
Dana: Proposed schedule: freeze SDK changes by 2025-04-25, internal canary 2025-05-01, partner canary 2025-05-15, announce deprecation 2025-05-30, remove header 2025-06-15. This gives ~6 weeks for partners after partner canary.
Alice: That seems reasonable and aligns with enterprise expectations. We need to make the allowlist request process clear in the partner portal and offer an emergency hotline for partners who encounter blockers.
Eva: Legal check: update contract annex and send partner notice template. I can turn around a draft by 2025-04-18.
deploy-bot: canary deployment queued for 2025-05-01 14:00 UTC — ID #canary-5742
Carlos: PartnerX asked for a per-request runtime header as escape-hatch (no SDK change). Ben already ok'd `X-RW-Legacy-Auth`. We'll need to document that it is monitored and will expire.
Ben: We'll also implement a server fallback: if new header missing, consult a short-lived KV mapping for legacy sessions for up to 30 days, and emit metric `rw-legacy-deprecation`. That reduces partner interruptions during rotation.
Dana: Marketing: coordinate the joint customer-facing launch note and marketplace listing change. PartnerX PM needs a sample deprecation notice to forward to their customers. Carlos, can you ping them and get their preferred send date?
Carlos: Pinged PartnerX PM (they're not in this channel). They asked for the draft today if possible.
Alice: I'll draft a short customer notice and post it here for review within 24 hours. Keep it concise: what, why, timeline, steps to migrate, support contacts.
Ben: Also, SDKs should surface a runtime warning log message and an SDK-level metric so partners can measure usage of legacy vs new.
Carlos: I'll add those metrics to the partner test plan. Thanks — this will reduce support load.
Dana: Let's reconvene next Thursday 10am PT to sign off on the comms and allowlist workflow.
Alice: Thanks all :thumbsup:
